summary: Healthcheck/monitoring pings billed on finalized invoice after promo credit applied
description: Issue summary: Customer (NimbleDocs) received a finalized monthly invoice that included a ~ $12 charge labeled 'healthcheck-ping' with token count 0. This occurred after a promotional credit was applied earlier in the cycle. Impact: Customer flagged unexpected charge and is asking for explanation and refund if charge is erroneous. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-east, monthly billing cycle ending 2026-03-01. Steps to reproduce (as reported): 1) Scheduled internal monitoring service issues periodic HTTP healthcheck pings to Redwood endpoint using a service key tagged 'monitoring'. 2) During billing cycle, a promo credit coupon was applied to the org on 2026-02-20 that zeroed out several lines. 3) Finalized invoice (2026-03-01) contains an extra line: 'healthcheck-ping' quantity 0, unit price $0.003, amount $11.97, invoice total nonzero despite visible promo credit lines. Expected behavior: Healthcheck or zero-token lines should either be suppressed from final invoice or correctly zeroed by promo-credit logic. Actual behavior: Line shows zero tokens but a nonzero charge; promo-credit appears to be applied after a rounding/aggregation step causing a residual amount. Logs/evidence: Customer attached PDF of invoice and example API key tags. Internal logs: postback receipts show healthchecks were ingested as 'probe' traffic on 2026-02-27 03:12-03:18 UTC, but token counter shows 0 tokens for those requests. Billing reconciler shows event hashes for those postbacks with nonempty rate_id and unit_price. Timeline: 2026-03-02 customer ticket opened. 2026-03-03 CS acknowledged, asked for invoice PDF and API key. 2026-03-04 SRE started investigation. 2026-03-10 reconciler engineer reproduced aggregation edge case locally.
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Thompson (CS): Thanks for filing this — can you attach the finalized invoice and the API key id used for the healthcheck activity? We've escalated to billing and SRE for triage.

2026-03-03 Customer (NimbleDocs - contact: Jose Alvarez): Attached invoice PDF (INV-2026-03-NIMBLE) and monitoring key id: mk_live_7f2a. Customer says monitoring pings are low priority and expects them to be suppressed for billing.

2026-03-04 Ethan Cole (SRE): Initial triage: I can see postbacks tagged as 'monitoring' were classified as 'probe' in ingestion, but reconciler assigned a rate_id and unit_price. Tokenization pipeline returned 0 tokens due to header-only probe. Investigating how reconciler handles promo credits and rounding.

2026-03-06 Billing Team (Lina Patel): Noted the invoice lines were subtotaled before promo-credit application. Promo credit applied at org-level rounding step; potential floating-point remainder left. Spawning reconciliation run against archived postbacks for that billing window.

2026-03-11 Ethan Cole (SRE): Reproducer: when a postback has unit_price > 0 and tokens == 0, rounding aggregation computes line_amount = unit_price * implied_unit_quantity (defaults to 1), then promo credit application subtracts discount at subtotal level, and the leftover rounding can remain positive. Patch proposed in PR 1428 to treat 0-token lines as non-billable and drop them pre-aggregation.

2026-03-12 Maya Thompson (CS): Provided customer with interim status and offered provisional credit while we complete fix. Customer accepted provisional credit and asked for final confirmation once invoice is adjusted.

2026-03-13 Billing (Lina Patel): Flagged that historical invoices need selective adjustment; prepared credit memo workflow for NimbleDocs for $11.97. Also scheduling post-release run to reprocess March window to prevent recurrence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Probe/healthcheck postbacks were tagged but not filtered from billing because token_count == 0 logic did not mark them as zero-charge in reconciler.
Hypothesis 2: Promo credit application occurs after line-level aggregation and rounding; small residuals can survive if a zero-token line was treated as quantity 1 at aggregation time.

Evidence: Local run of reconciler on archived bucket reproduced nonzero dollar amount when simulating probe postbacks with unit_price set in catalog. Reconciler logs (reconciler-2026-02-28.log) show 'tokens=0, rate_applied=true, quantity=1'.
Scope: We scanned 125 tenants in us-east with '_monitor' or 'health' tags and found 9 tenants with similar artifacts in the same cycle. NimbleDocs is the first to surface complaint.

Temporary mitigation: Add a reconciler rule to ignore any postback with tokens==0 AND tag in [monitor, healthcheck, probe] until code fix lands. This rule has been applied to production reconciler config on 2026-03-12.

Code change: PR github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/1428 updates billing aggregator to: (a) treat zero-token lines as zero-quantity, (b) apply promo credits at line-level where possible to avoid residual rounding, (c) add unit tests covering floating-point edge cases.
resolution: Provisional credit: Applied immediate credit memo of $11.97 to NimbleDocs (credit memo CM-2026-03-NIMBLE) pending reprocessed invoice; customer has accepted provisional credit.

Fix deployed: Merged PR 1428 and deployed reconciler change to staging on 2026-03-12 and to prod on 2026-03-13. Change ensures tokens==0 lines are dropped before aggregation and promo-credit rebalancing is performed at line-level.
Follow-up: Reprocess March billing window for affected tenants in us-east to remove similar residual charges; estimated rerun completion by 2026-03-17.
Runbook update: Added guidance to billing runbook 'Ignore zero-token probe lines' and created an alert for any invoice line with quantity==0 and amount>0.
Customer communication: Sent summary and credit confirmation to Jose Alvarez on 2026-03-13. Scheduled a short postmortem update on 2026-03-18 if rerun yields additional adjustments.
